objective: Build two winter traffic engines before demand arrives: Michigan Ice for water-specific ice-condition intent and Michigan XC for planning plus a controlled live-conditions tool. Score usefulness, search capture, freshness, differentiation, trust, maintainability, and retention instead of shipping isolated features.

dimensions.definition: Own distinct Michigan winter queries with indexable, non-cannibalizing search surfaces.
Help a visitor make the next real decision quickly rather than merely presenting data.
Use current authoritative or clearly bounded modeled observations where they materially improve the decision.
Cover enough Michigan waters/trails and local differences to create a meaningful long-tail moat.
Show source, recency, limitations, and off-season/no-data states honestly.
Compose data and local context into something stronger than a directory or raw feed.
Never convert weather/model signals into unsupported grooming or ice-safety claims.
Give a useful next step into the other winter product or authority surface without keyword cannibalization.

fatalPenalties.trigger: Any claim that modeled, weather, satellite, camera, or remote data makes ice safe or verifies local thickness.
Any claim that a trail is open/groomed/skiable today based only on weather or snow data rather than an operator/groomer report.
Changing the xcski production deployment if source or Git-to-deployment ownership is later lost or ambiguous.
Editing generated Michigan Ice HTML rather than its generator and regenerating outputs.
Breaking canonical/indexability or creating competing URLs for the same primary intent.
Presenting parent-Great-Lake satellite ice cover as a measurement of a specific bay or fishing location.
Presenting live-looking data without timestamps, no-data handling, or source transparency.

baseline.sourceWindow: Google Search Console export through 2026-08-13 plus repository/product audit on 2026-08-18

largestLosses: Search visibility is far behind the quality of the product.
Only six water-specific search surfaces exist despite strong local differences.
The next-step winter handoff is present but not prominent on water pages.

xc.penaltyReason: Historical baseline: live XC source and deployment ownership had not yet been recovered.
largestLosses: Live source/deployment ownership was not recovered.
Grooming truth remained fragmented across operators and community reports.
The planning hub needed a faster comparison layer and clearer source hierarchy.

evidence: Generator adds a statewide six-water behavior matrix so visitors compare depth/current/exposure before comparing numbers.
Every generated water page receives three unique local decision questions grounded in that water's existing behavior and data limits.
Existing ACIS, NWS, GLERL, cameras, timestamps, off-season states, and safety language remain intact.
Every water page and the hub gain an explicit winter handoff to the XC planner/live snow signal without creating a competing ice URL.
Generated outputs remain checksum-protected and dateModified advances through the generator rather than a hand edit.
Claude recovered the byte-identical 48-trail production artifact into izworskic/xcski with recorded SHA-256 provenance.
The recovered repo now deploys through Vercel from GitHub and post-merge status is green on the hardened production build.
The live deploy output keeps Open-Meteo snow depth, 72-hour snowfall, and trailhead temperature but removes model-derived claims that imply grooming, opening, or skiability.
All 48 trail cards retain operator or land-manager verification links as final trail-status truth and the regional model signal carries a Michigan-time freshness stamp.
The main-domain authority hub remains the planning/search owner while xcski remains the live-conditions tool, with measured handoffs in both directions and no competing XC URL.

xcControlledSurface.note: XC source and Git-to-Vercel ownership are recovered; no orphan penalty remains.

activeSeasonOutcomeTargets.principle: Use preseason scores as build-quality gates. Search Console outcomes and first-party behavior remain the real market test once winter demand arrives.
